question: Which of the following causes of malabsorption occurs with alteration of the intestinal mucosa ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Celiac disease" -> "immune response to gluten" -> "damage to intestinal mucosa" -> "malabsorption of nutrients" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Achalasia" -> "esophageal motility disorder" -> "difficulty swallowing" -> "not primarily affecting intestinal mucosa" -> "unclear" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Cholestasis" -> "bile flow obstruction" -> "impaired fat absorption" -> "not directly altering intestinal mucosa" -> "unclear" -> 65%
CHAIN: "Crigler-Najjar syndrome" -> "disorder of bilirubin metabolism" -> "not related to intestinal mucosa" -> "no alteration of intestinal mucosa" -> " -> 0%
enhanced_information: Celiac disease is characterized by an immune response to gluten, leading to damage of the intestinal mucosa and resulting in malabsorption of nutrients, which aligns with consensus understanding. In contrast, achalasia is primarily an esophageal motility disorder that does not directly affect the intestinal mucosa, thus it is not a cause of malabsorption related to mucosal alteration. Cholestasis involves bile flow obstruction, impairing fat absorption but does not directly alter the intestinal mucosa. Crigler-Najjar syndrome is a metabolic disorder unrelated to the intestinal mucosa and does not cause malabsorption. Therefore, the only option that causes malabsorption through alteration of the intestinal mucosa is celiac disease.
analysis: Celiac disease is well-established in medical literature as a condition that leads to malabsorption due to an immune-mediated response to gluten, which results in damage to the intestinal mucosa. This damage impairs the absorption of nutrients, making it a clear cause of malabsorption associated with alteration of the intestinal mucosa. In contrast, the other options do not directly cause changes to the intestinal mucosa: Crigler-Najjar syndrome is a metabolic disorder affecting bilirubin metabolism, cholestasis involves bile flow issues affecting fat absorption but not the mucosa itself, and achalasia is primarily an esophageal motility disorder. Therefore, the most likely correct answer is celiac disease, as it directly correlates with the alteration of the intestinal mucosa leading to malabsorption.
